name: Disinfectants and sanitizers (EPA-registered antimicrobial sprays, wipes, concentrates)
governing_basis: EPA-registered antimicrobial products (US FIFRA) are a distinct testing bucket. The FIFRA Confidential Statement of Formula and the antimicrobial active ingredient govern registration; any metal-based active (e.g., silver, copper) is a DECLARED ACTIVE, not a contaminant, and is outside the HMTc contaminant panel. No FIFRA or FDA sanitizing-solution instrument sets a heavy-metal contaminant maximum for the product. Heavy-metal contaminants take the consumer-chemical read-across (NMPA 2015); organotin is screened per REACH entry 20 given the historical organotin-biocide pathway. Basis: total content in the product as placed on the market.
native_basis_label: total heavy-metal content in product as placed on the market (mg/kg product)
scope_note: EPA-registered antimicrobial products under FIFRA (sprays, wipes, concentrates) - a distinct testing bucket. Metal-based actives (silver, copper) are declared actives, not contaminants, and are outside the HMTc contaminant panel. Organotin is screened per REACH entry 20 given the historical organotin-biocide pathway. No FIFRA/FDA instrument sets a heavy-metal contaminant maximum for the product.

Pb.basis: total lead content, product as placed on the market (mg/kg)
Pb.label: Read across from China NMPA 2015 mandatory cosmetic lead limit (10 mg/kg), conservative for a residue/incidental-dermal antimicrobial product. No FIFRA/FDA heavy-metal contaminant ML exists for antimicrobial products.

tAs.basis: total arsenic content, product as placed on the market (mg/kg)
tAs.label: Read across from China NMPA 2015 mandatory cosmetic total-arsenic limit (2 mg/kg). No FIFRA/FDA heavy-metal contaminant ML exists for antimicrobial products.

iAs.rationale: No jurisdiction sets an inorganic-arsenic limit for antimicrobial cleaning products; the consumer-chemical trace-metal instruments regulate TOTAL arsenic (see the tAs cell), which bounds the inorganic fraction (iAs <= tAs). No routed occurrence source measured or speciated inorganic arsenic in these products.
iAs.regulatory_basis: Bounded by the total-arsenic read-across ceiling (NMPA 2015, 2 mg/kg); no inorganic-arsenic limit for antimicrobial products in any jurisdiction
iAs.jurisdictions_checked: US EPA FIFRA; US FDA 21 CFR 178.1010; CN GB 14930.1; CN NMPA 2015; EU BPR; EU REACH Annex XVII; Health Canada
iAs.cross_sourced: parent tAs published (NMPA read-across) + credible-ML register checked 2026-08-13 (no iAs antimicrobial-product limit); occurrence corpus measured no arsenic speciation
iAs.reference_method: Total-arsenic screen by ICP-MS; reflex inorganic-arsenic speciation only if total arsenic approaches the read-across ceiling.

Cd.basis: total cadmium content, product as placed on the market (mg/kg)
Cd.label: Read across from China NMPA 2015 mandatory cosmetic cadmium limit (5 mg/kg). No FIFRA/FDA heavy-metal contaminant ML exists for antimicrobial products.

tHg.basis: total mercury content, product as placed on the market (mg/kg)
tHg.label: Read across from China NMPA 2015 mandatory cosmetic mercury limit (1 mg/kg). Note: mercurial biocides (e.g. phenylmercuric compounds) are prohibited in antimicrobial products; this cell is a contaminant ceiling. No FIFRA/FDA heavy-metal contaminant ML exists for antimicrobial products.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury has no formation or migration pathway in an antimicrobial formulation; it is a marine-bioaccumulation speciation. The consumer-chemical mercury instruments regulate total mercury (see the tHg cell), which bounds any organomercury fraction. No routed occurrence source measured or speciated methylmercury in these products.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: Bounded by the total-mercury read-across ceiling (NMPA 2015, 1 mg/kg); no methylmercury limit for antimicrobial products in any jurisdiction
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: US EPA FIFRA; US FDA 21 CFR 178.1010; CN GB 14930.1; CN NMPA 2015; EU BPR; EU REACH Annex XVII; Health Canada
MeHg.cross_sourced: parent tHg published (NMPA read-across) + credible-ML register checked 2026-08-13 (no MeHg antimicrobial-product limit); occurrence corpus screened, no organomercury speciation reported
MeHg.reference_method: Total-mercury screen by CV-AAS or ICP-MS; no reflex methylmercury speciation defined (no formation pathway).

Ni.reference_method: Total nickel by ICP-MS on the product as placed on market (acid digestion).
Ni.escalation_rule: Nickel is a confirmed dermal sensitizer and is measured in household cleaning products (ecetoc1992). No jurisdiction sets a numeric total-nickel maximum for antimicrobial products, so certification screens total nickel and escalates a lot above the running category control band to ALARA review.
Ni.rationale: Present in the occurrence corpus; no sovereign ML in a consumer-chemical total-content basis.

Al.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS on the product as placed on market.
Al.escalation_rule: Aluminium is Tier-2 and may be a functional ingredient. No jurisdiction sets an antimicrobial-product aluminium maximum. Screen total aluminium; a lot outside the functional-ingredient expectation triggers ingredient review.
Al.rationale: No sovereign ML; potential functional-ingredient source means a not-material claim would be false. Screen, do not publish a number.

Cr-total.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on the product as placed on market.
Cr-total.escalation_rule: Total chromium is measured in cleaning products (ecetoc1992). No jurisdiction sets an antimicrobial-product chromium maximum. Screen total chromium and reflex Cr(VI) speciation where total chromium is elevated or the formulation is oxidizing/acidic.
Cr-total.rationale: Present in the occurrence corpus; no sovereign ML in a consumer-chemical total-content basis.

Cr-VI.reference_method: Hexavalent chromium by IC-ICP-MS with alkaline extraction (US EPA 3060A / 7199).
Cr-VI.escalation_rule: Cr(VI) is measured in some consumer cleaning products (ecetoc1992) and oxidizing antimicrobial chemistries (hypochlorite, peroxides) can stabilize it. No jurisdiction sets an antimicrobial-product Cr(VI) maximum. Reflex Cr(VI) speciation on oxidizing formulations and where total chromium is elevated; escalate a positive Cr(VI) result to ALARA review.
Cr-VI.rationale: Measured in the corpus; a real hazard on oxidizing chemistries; no sovereign number, so a method + escalation rule is published rather than an invented threshold.

Sn.reference_method: Organotin speciation (DBT/DOT/TBT as Sn) by GC-ICP-MS or GC-MS, plus total inorganic tin by ICP-MS.
Sn.escalation_rule: Some antimicrobial products historically used organotin biocides; REACH Annex XVII entry 20 restricts organotin in consumer articles. Screen organotin on antimicrobial products and escalate any organotin detection; inorganic tin has no formulation source and is verified periodically.
Sn.rationale: Antimicrobial products are the one cleaning sub-scope with a plausible organotin (biocide) pathway, so tin is screened here rather than treated not-material as in the other sub-pathways.

method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default, consumer-chemical form; native basis = total heavy-metal content in product as placed on market, mg/kg; no cross-basis min)
